questions.text: Per Lec 5.1, unchecked population growth most directly intensifies which environmental pressure bundle?

choices.text: Higher demand for food and fiber plus more pollution, waste, and ecosystem degradation
Exclusive reduction of urban air pollutants without resource demand
Elimination of survival-driven human behavior toward the environment
Guaranteed stabilization of pest and disease rates in dense cities

questions.expl: Correct (a): slides link more people to resource demand and pollution/waste/degradation. (b)–(d) contradict the lecture chain.

questions.text: In population ecology (Lec 5.1), a population is defined as:

choices.text: Any mixed-species assemblage in a biome regardless of place or time
A group of interacting individuals of the same kind in the same place at the same time
Only humans enumerated in a national census year
The total biomass of producers minus consumers in a food web

questions.expl: Correct (b): matches the lecture definition (same kind, place, time). (a) drops species identity. (c) narrows to humans only. (d) is ecosystem metabolism, not population ecology.

questions.text: A population with a large proportion of young individuals relative to adults is characterized in the slides as:

choices.text: A declining population
A stable population
A growing population
A population with zero natality

questions.expl: Correct (c): age-structure slide labels many young → growing population. (a) is the opposite pattern. (b) requires young ≈ adults. (d) denies births.

questions.text: Absolute population density in Lec 5.1 refers to:

choices.text: The number of individuals in relation to all other species in the community
The actual count of individuals per unit area (per unit time in the definition)
Only the crude birth rate per 1,000 persons
The logistic carrying capacity K exclusively

questions.expl: Correct (b): absolute density = actual count. (a) defines relative density. (c) is a vital rate. (d) is a model parameter, not the density definition.

questions.text: Per Lec 5.1, high population density can increase crowding, competition, mortality, and pest or disease pressure.
questions.expl: TRUE: lecture lists crowding, inconvenience, competition, retarded growth, increased mortality, and rapid pest/disease increase under high density. FALSE would deny documented density effects.

questions.text: Low population density in the lecture is associated with which outcome pairing?

choices.text: Larger individuals and increased reproduction with more available resources
Mandatory exponential growth with unlimited resources forever
Zero survivorship at all age classes
Uniform spatial distribution only in urban NCR

questions.expl: Correct (a): low-density slide bullets. (b) misstates growth models. (c) contradicts survivorship concept. (d) confuses spatial pattern with density effects.

questions.text: Which method for estimating density of mobile animals is named in Lec 5.1?

choices.text: Capture-recapture
Nephelometric turbidity standardization
Biochemical oxygen demand proxy
Ice–albedo positive feedback

questions.expl: Correct (a): capture-recapture listed with census and sampling. (b)–(d) belong to water quality or climate topics.

questions.text: According to Lec 5.1 (2020 PSA figure cited), Manila’s population density is approximately:

choices.text: 363 persons per square kilometer (national average)
73,920 persons per square kilometer
2,847 persons per square kilometer (provincial Cavite figure)
109 persons per square kilometer (MIMAROPA regional figure)

questions.expl: Correct (b): slide cites Manila as most densely populated city at 73,920 persons/km² (2020, PSA). (a) is national density. (c) is Cavite province. (d) is MIMAROPA.

questions.text: Spatial distribution patterns enumerated in Lec 5.1 include:

choices.text: Random, uniform (regular), and clumped (aggregated)
Only circadian and tidal rhythms
Exponential, logistic, and carrying-capacity only
Point source, non-point source, and leachate

questions.expl: Correct (a): spatial distribution trio from population ecology slides. (b) is temporal distribution. (c) names growth curves. (d) is pollution-source taxonomy.

questions.text: Natality as taught in Lec 5.1 is best described as:

choices.text: Production of new individuals by birth, hatching, germination, or cloning
The percentage of individuals surviving to each age class
Number of deaths per 1,000 population per year only
Physical inability to reproduce under any circumstances

questions.expl: Correct (a): natality definition on slides. (b) is survivorship. (c) is mortality framing. (d) confuses fecundity limits with natality.

questions.text: Fecundity versus fertility in Lec 5.1 is distinguished as:

choices.text: Fecundity = physical ability to reproduce; fertility = actual offspring produced
Fecundity = deaths per unit time; fertility = immigration rate
Both terms mean identical census counts
Fecundity = life span; fertility = life expectancy

questions.expl: Correct (a): slide pairing. (b) mislabels vital rates. (c) collapses distinct concepts. (d) mixes longevity metrics.

questions.text: Crude birth rate in the lecture is defined as:

choices.text: Number of born individuals per 1,000 individuals at a given time
Number of individuals per square kilometer only
Intrinsic rate r in the logistic equation exclusively
Years an individual is expected to continue living at a given age

questions.expl: Correct (a): crude birth rate per 1,000. (b) is density. (c) is growth-rate parameter. (d) is life expectancy.

questions.text: Per Lec 5.1, exponential (geometric) population growth is density-independent and can produce a J-shaped curve when resources are effectively unlimited for a short period.
questions.expl: TRUE: slides state dN/dt = rN under stable/unlimited conditions with J-shaped pattern; logistic growth is density-dependent. FALSE would swap model properties.

questions.text: Logistic population growth in Lec 5.1 is characterized by:

choices.text: dN/dt = rN with no upper limit ever
dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K, slowing as density approaches carrying capacity K
Zero mortality at all ages
Only temporal distribution (circadian) patterns

questions.expl: Correct (b): logistic equation and density-dependent slowdown in slides. (a) is exponential form. (c) is unrealistic. (d) is unrelated.

questions.text: In the squirrel example (Lec 5.1), N₀ = 500 in 2023 with r = 2.5% per year, N₂₀ in 2043 is approximately:

choices.text: 350 units
500 units
824 units
1,411 million units

questions.expl: Correct (c): slide calculation N₂₀ = 500·e^(0.025×20) ≈ 824. (a) is the backward-projection starting population in the second example. (b) ignores growth. (d) confuses with national population ranks.

questions.text: When population drops from 500 to 350 over five years in the lecture’s reverse example, the implied annual growth rate r is about:
questions.expl: Correct (c): slide solves ln(350/500) = −5r → r ≈ 0.071 (7.1%). (a) is the forward squirrel rate. (b) is world growth cited elsewhere. (d) is a doubling-time misread.

questions.text: World population figures in Lec 5.1 (April 2023) include approximately:

choices.text: 7.9 billion people with an estimated growth rate near 0.94%
3.0 billion people with 7.1% annual growth
114.1 million people ranking first globally
76.5 million people as the 2026 UN median

questions.expl: Correct (a): ~7.9B and 0.94% growth from slides. (b) misstates scale/rate. (c) is Philippines-scale. (d) is an older PH baseline year.

questions.text: In the 2018 country ranking slide, the Philippines is listed at rank 12 with a population of about:
questions.expl: Correct (a): PH row in lecture table. (b) is China. (c) is United States. (d) is Manila density, not national population.

questions.text: Top three regions by population size in the 2020 census (Lec 5.1) are:

choices.text: CALABARZON, National Capital Region, and Central Luzon
BARMM, MIMAROPA, and CAR only
Western Visayas, Ilocos, and Batanes exclusively
China, India, and Indonesia within the Philippines

questions.expl: Correct (a): CALABARZON (16.2M), NCR, Central Luzon named as top three. (b) lists sparse regions. (c) is incomplete. (d) confuses countries with regions.

questions.text: If the Philippine annual population growth rate remains near 1.47% (2023 figure in lecture), the slides estimate doubling in roughly 47 years.
questions.expl: TRUE: lecture states ~47 years to double at 1.47%. FALSE would contradict the stated doubling-time pedagogy.

questions.text: National population density in Lec 5.1 is given as about 363 persons/km², while NCR’s density is about:

choices.text: 21,765 persons/km²
977 persons/km²
93 persons/km²
73,920 persons/km²

questions.expl: Correct (a): NCR = 21,765 vs national 363 in slides. (b) is CALABARZON. (c) is Batanes sparsity. (d) is Manila city metric.

questions.text: Average Filipino household size in Lec 5.1 declined to about _____ in 2020 from 5.07 persons in 1995.

choices.text: 4.1 persons
5.9 persons
7.9 persons
1.63 persons

questions.expl: Correct (a): 4.1 persons average household (2020). (b) is BARMM largest regional average. (c) confuses with world population billions. (d) is a growth-rate figure.

questions.text: Integrated lesson from Lec 5.1: the Philippines holding many of the world’s densest cities implies that local environmental crises (pollution, waste, habitat pressure) are amplified because:

choices.text: High human density concentrates resource demand and waste generation on limited land
Population density automatically eliminates disease and pest outbreaks
Logistic growth never applies to urban populations
Natality and mortality cease to affect age structure in cities

questions.expl: Correct (a): ties density effects to the syllabus arc toward pollution and waste topics. (b)–(d) contradict lecture ecology and demography.

questions.text: Which definition best matches the lecture’s concept of pollution?

choices.text: Undesirable change in physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of an ecosystem diminishing resource quality and utility
Any increase in rainfall intensity during monsoon seasons only
Exclusive legal term for solid waste in RA 9003 only
Natural volcanic ash that always improves soil fertility without trade-offs

questions.expl: Correct (a): slides define pollution as undesirable environmental change reducing resource utility. (b) narrows to weather. (c) mislabels a single statute domain. (d) ignores harm pathways stressed in class.

questions.text: Under Water Code Article 10 (as summarized in Lec 5.2), water appropriation purposes include which grouping?

choices.text: Domestic, municipal, irrigation, power generation, fisheries, livestock, industrial, recreational, and other purposes
Only hydroelectric export to neighboring states without domestic use
Exclusive bottled-water franchising without agricultural allocation
Military bases only, excluding irrigation and fisheries

questions.expl: Correct (a): mirrors the enumerated appropriation classes in the lecture list. (b)–(d) omit or misstate the multi-sector appropriation frame.
refs: Philippine Water Code — Article 10 appropriation purposes

questions.text: Global freshwater use shares cited in the lecture allocate approximately what fractions to agriculture, industry, and domestic uses?

choices.text: 70% agriculture · 20% industry · 10% domestic
10% agriculture · 70% industry · 20% domestic
33% each sector
90% domestic · 10% agriculture · 0% industry

questions.expl: Correct (a): matches the 70/20/10 pedagogy slide. (b)–(d) invert or flatten the distribution taught in-session.

questions.text: Turbidity in drinking-water quality monitoring is best described as:

choices.text: Light-scattering by suspended/colloidal material; reported in NTU via nephelometric methods
Direct count of fecal coliform colonies per 100 mL only
Measure of dissolved oxygen saturation at 25 °C exclusively
Mass of lead per liter without optical inference

questions.expl: Correct (a): lecture ties turbidity to silica-standardized NTU and nephelometers. (b) is microbiological. (c) is DO. (d) is a metals metric.

questions.text: Dissolved oxygen (DO) in aquatic systems is characterized in the slides as:

choices.text: Oxygen available to aquatic life; higher concentrations generally indicate better quality for ecosystems
Primary direct cause of cholera outbreaks in all waters
Identical to biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)
Unrelated to temperature or biological metabolism

questions.expl: Correct (a): DO supports aquatic organisms; slides note flat taste at very low DO for drinking. (b) overstates disease causation. (c) confuses DO with BOD. (d) ignores temperature coupling taught later.

questions.text: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is used in class primarily as:

choices.text: An indirect measure of biodegradable organic matter that microbes oxidize while consuming oxygen
A direct measure of heavy-metal toxicity in sediments
The same parameter as nephelometric turbidity
A radiation dose standard for nuclear effluents only

questions.expl: Correct (a): BOD proxies organics via microbial O₂ demand. (b)–(d) misassign parameters.

questions.text: Which pairing distinguishes point from non-point water pollution sources in Lec 5.2?

choices.text: Point: discrete discharge such as a pipe; non-point: diffuse runoff/leachate without a single outlet
Point: only rainfall; non-point: only volcanic eruptions
Point: exclusively agricultural; non-point: exclusively industrial stacks
Both terms describe identical pipe discharges

questions.expl: Correct (a): matches pipe example vs agricultural runoff/leachate framing. (b)–(d) invert or collapse categories.

questions.text: Eutrophication, as presented, is chiefly driven by:

choices.text: Nutrient accumulation (e.g., N/P) leading to algal blooms and oxygen stress when organics decompose
Excess dissolved oxygen from over-aeration alone
Complete absence of sediments in all lakes
Thermal cooling of power plants that raises DO indefinitely

questions.expl: Correct (a): nutrient enrichment → blooms → organic loading → BOD/DO impacts. (b)–(d) contradict lecture mechanisms.

questions.text: Suspended sediments in surface waters can harm aquatic systems by:

choices.text: Reducing light penetration, smothering spawning habitat, and damaging eggs/fry
Increasing photosynthesis at all depths uniformly
Eliminating need for turbidity measurement
Guaranteeing higher dissolved oxygen through shading alone

questions.expl: Correct (a): sedimentation effects in slides include spawning damage and light limits. (b)–(d) misstate impacts.

questions.text: Thermal pollution to receiving waters is described as:

choices.text: Raising temperature, lowering DO solubility, and increasing metabolic rates—risking shock or stress in organisms
Always beneficial because heat eliminates all pathogens instantly
Unrelated to dissolved oxygen chemistry
Only a groundwater issue with no surface-water relevance

questions.expl: Correct (a): couples temperature–DO–metabolism and thermal shock narrative. (b)–(d) contradict lecture content.

questions.text: Which disease–agent pairing is correctly associated with waterborne transmission in the lecture list?

choices.text: Typhoid fever — bacterial
Typhoid fever — solely viral hepatitis without bacterial forms
Schistosomiasis — purely photochemical oxidant
Cholera — non-infectious ergonomic injury

questions.expl: Correct (a): typhoid listed as bacterial waterborne. (b) mislabels. (c) schistosomiasis is parasitic worm per slides. (d) is absurd.

questions.text: The Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water (PNSDW) in the lecture are attributed to:

choices.text: DOH guidelines (1963 origin in slides) covering source-to-tap physical, chemical, and microbiological parameters
BFP fire-code inspection forms exclusively
TIA-568 cabling performance only
UNFCCC NDC templates only

questions.expl: Correct (a): PNSDW scope as taught. (b)–(d) are unrelated regimes.
refs: Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water (DOH)

questions.text: DENR Administrative Order No. 34 (1990) is summarized as establishing:

choices.text: Water use classification and water-quality criteria/standards for beneficial uses including domestic, agricultural, and industrial classes
Exclusive air-quality NAAQS for Metro Manila only
Mining tailings bonds without water classes
A ban on all irrigation withdrawals nationally

questions.expl: Correct (a): AO 34 classification/standards narrative. (b) is air law. (c)/(d) are not AO 34 functions.
refs: DENR Administrative Order No. 34, Series of 1990

questions.text: In DENR AO 34 freshwater classes, Class AA is designated for:

choices.text: Public Water Supply Class I
Agricultural supply only
Industrial Class II exclusively
Recreational contact without supply uses

questions.expl: Correct (a): Class AA = public water supply class I in slide taxonomy. (b)–(d) mis-assign classes.
refs: DENR Administrative Order No. 34, Series of 1990

questions.text: Republic Act No. 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004) is characterized in lecture as:

choices.text: Comprehensive water-quality management targeting land-based pollution sources; signed March 2004, effective May 2004
Repealing RA 9003 solid waste law entirely
A 1978 PEISS impact-statement statute
Regulating only stratospheric ozone-depleting substances

questions.expl: Correct (a): RA 9275 dates and land-based pollution focus per slides. (b)–(d) misidentify statutes/domains.

questions.text: Solids in water are differentiated in class by:

choices.text: Suspended solids retained on a standard filter vs dissolved solids passing through with the filtrate
Color vs odor only without physical separation
Radioactivity vs turbidity as identical measures
BOD vs NTU as the same test

questions.expl: Correct (a): glass-fiber filter partition taught in slides. (b)–(d) confuse parameters.

questions.text: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) in water supplies is noted for:

choices.text: Rotten-egg odor associated with decaying organic deposits in some groundwaters
Sweet floral scent indicating pristine alpine water always
Proof of zero biological activity
Replacing chlorine disinfection legally in all utilities

questions.expl: Correct (a): H₂S odor pathway in lecture. (b)–(d) contradict slide examples.

questions.text: pH and alkalinity monitoring in water treatment contexts serve to:

choices.text: Control treatment processes; alkalinity buffers acid addition while pH measures acidity/alkalinity intensity
Replace all microbiological testing
Measure wind speed over reservoirs
Eliminate need for corrosion control on metals

questions.expl: Correct (a): treatment control + alkalinity/acidity definitions from slides. (b)–(d) overstate or misassign roles.

questions.text: Inorganic chemical pollutants highlighted include metals such as:

choices.text: Mercury and lead among toxic metals listed
Only biodegradable sugars
Only household compost humus
Neon and argon as primary water toxics

questions.expl: Correct (a): slides list Hg, Pb, etc. (b)–(d) misclassify pollutant types.

questions.text: Leachate from waste deposits is classified in lecture as a:

choices.text: Non-point source pathway carrying contaminants via runoff/groundwater
Point source identical to a single stack height
Natural volcanic product only
Parameter identical to nephelometric turbidity

questions.expl: Correct (a): leachate under non-point/discussed runoff framing. (b)–(d) mislabel.

questions.text: Higher BOD in a river reach generally signals more biodegradable organics available to microbes, tending to depress dissolved oxygen unless re-aeration keeps pace.
questions.expl: TRUE: lecture links organic loading → microbial O₂ consumption → lower DO for aquatic life. FALSE would deny the central BOD narrative.

questions.text: Parasitic organisms in the lecture’s biological water-quality taxonomy include:

choices.text: Worms among the five listed groups (with bacteria, protozoa, viruses, fungi)
Only photochemical oxidants
Only asbestos fibers
Only carbon monoxide from garages

questions.expl: Correct (a): five-type list includes worms. (b)–(d) are air/indoor pollutants or wrong kingdom.

questions.text: Primary causes of water pollution enumerated in Lec 5.2 include which set?

choices.text: Industrial wastes, oil spills, sewage, marine dumping, leaking landfills, pesticides/fertilizers, and animal waste among others
Only lightning strikes on reservoirs
Only stratospheric ozone thinning
Only indoor formaldehyde off-gassing

questions.expl: Correct (a): mirrors slide bullet list of primary causes. (b)–(d) import unrelated mechanisms.

questions.text: The lecture cites WHO-scale mortality associated with ambient air pollution at roughly:

choices.text: Seven million premature deaths per year worldwide
Seven hundred deaths globally per decade
Zero attributable deaths if PM is visible
Only indoor radon without outdoor PM effects

questions.expl: Correct (a): opening WHO statistic in slides. (b)–(d) contradict or trivialize the figure.
refs: WHO Global Ambient Air Quality Database (cited in lecture)

questions.text: Clean dry air composition in the lecture lists nitrogen and oxygen at approximately:

choices.text: 50% N₂ and 50% O₂
100% O₂ with trace argon only
0.03% N₂ and 99% CO₂

questions.expl: Correct (a): table values from slides. (b)–(d) misstate atmospheric composition.

questions.text: Weather and climate phenomena emphasized in class occur primarily in which atmospheric layer?

choices.text: Troposphere (roughly up to 10–18 km in slides)
Exosphere only
Mesosphere exclusively for daily rain
Thermosphere as the sole pollution sink

questions.expl: Correct (a): troposphere hosts weather/climate per lecture. (b)–(d) misplace processes.

questions.text: Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) in urban smog is described as:

choices.text: Contributing to brownish haze and aggravating respiratory illness; linked to fossil combustion
A noble gas filling balloons harmlessly
The dominant stratospheric ozone shield gas in all contexts
Unrelated to vehicles or power plants

questions.expl: Correct (a): NOx/smog health and color narrative. (b)–(d) misidentify chemistry/sources.

questions.text: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) sources and effects in lecture include:

choices.text: Combustion in power plants/refineries; respiratory aggravation; corrosion and visibility loss at sufficient concentrations
Only natural photosynthesis byproduct with no health effects
Exclusive indoor radon decay chain
Primary constituent of clean dry air at 78%

questions.expl: Correct (a): SO₂ sources and impacts as taught. (b)–(d) contradict slide content.

questions.text: Suspended particulate matter in air pollution discourse is tied to:

choices.text: Cardiovascular and respiratory harm; toxic constituents such as benzene, arsenic, asbestos, and lead noted in slides
Only beneficial cooling of urban heat islands without health trade-offs
Exclusive elimination of greenhouse gases
Only dissolved oxygen deficits in rivers

questions.expl: Correct (a): PM health/toxic fraction lecture points. (b)–(d) are wrong media or mechanisms.

questions.text: Photochemical smog requires which condition per Lec 5.3?

choices.text: Sunlight-driven chemical reactions among precursors
Exclusive indoor mothball off-gassing without outdoor chemistry
Subsurface groundwater leachate only
Sediment deposition in reservoirs only

questions.expl: Correct (a): photochemical smog defined by solar-driven chemistry. (b)–(d) are other pollution types.

questions.text: Components of photochemical smog listed include:

choices.text: Tropospheric ozone, nitric acid, formaldehyde, and PAN among others
Only methane from rice paddies without oxidants
Only fecal coliform bacteria
Only turbidity measured in NTU

questions.expl: Correct (a): smog component list in slides. (b)–(d) misassign pollutants/parameters.

questions.text: The greenhouse effect in lecture is defined as:

choices.text: Atmospheric gases trapping infrared radiation, contributing to global warming/climate change
Visible smog that eliminates all UV instantly
Only acid rain formation in lakes
Exclusive indoor asbestos hazard

questions.expl: Correct (a): IR trapping narrative with GHGs named (CO₂, CH₄, etc.). (b)–(d) confuse phenomena.

questions.text: COVID-19 lockdown air-quality observations in Metro Manila included:

choices.text: Temporary drops in NO₂ and PM₂.₅ with traffic/industry curbs, later rebounding as restrictions eased
Permanent elimination of all biomass burning in Central Luzon forever
Proof that pollution never returns after one quiet month
Exclusive increase in stratospheric ozone without tropospheric effects

questions.expl: Correct (a): temporary improvement + rebound stressed in slides. (b)–(d) overstate or misplace outcomes.
refs: UP Diliman Information Office (cited in lecture)

questions.text: An Air Quality Index (AQI) value of 100 in the lecture framing generally means:

choices.text: Pollutant level at the national air-quality standard protective of public health
Hazardous conditions for the entire population
Zero pollutants detected with perfect mountain air always
Identical to water BOD of 100 mg/L

questions.expl: Correct (a): AQI 100 ↔ standard level pedagogy (US EPA style explanation in slides). (b) is higher bands. (c) is unrealistic. (d) confuses media.

questions.text: AQI category 'Unhealthy' in the slide table corresponds roughly to which numeric range?
questions.expl: Correct (a): unhealthy band per lecture table. (b) is Good. (c) is Moderate. (d) is Hazardous.

questions.text: Acid rain formation in class involves atmospheric conversion of sulfur and nitrogen oxides into:

choices.text: Sulfuric and nitric acids lowering rain pH below natural ~5.6 background
Pure distilled water at pH 14 always
Only sodium chloride aerosols
Only biodegradable organics measured as BOD

questions.expl: Correct (a): acid rain chemistry and pH contrast (5.6 vs ~2.0 extreme example). (b)–(d) misstate products/parameters.

questions.text: Ecological damages from acid rain noted in lecture include:

choices.text: Forest soil-nutrient leaching and aquatic acidification harming fish
Guaranteed coral reef expansion from lower pH
Increased stratospheric ozone uniformly
Elimination of all smog precursors

questions.expl: Correct (a): soil leaching + lake acidification bullets. (b)–(d) contradict impacts taught.

questions.text: Classic smog etymology in the slides combines:

choices.text: Smoke and fog into a visible urban haze
Sodium and fluorine only
Sediment and leachate only
Turbidity and BOD only

questions.expl: Correct (a): smoke + fog definition. (b)–(d) are unrelated portmanteaus/parameters.

questions.text: Indoor air pollution is characterized as potentially:

choices.text: More concentrated than outdoor air in homes/offices for some pollutants
Always cleaner than any outdoor location by definition
Unrelated to asbestos or formaldehyde
Only a rural issue without urban cases

questions.expl: Correct (a): indoor can exceed outdoor per lecture warning. (b)–(d) contradict examples (asbestos, formaldehyde, smoke).

questions.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) indoor risks in lecture stem from:

choices.text: Odorless combustion products (heaters, poorly vented garages, tobacco smoke) impairing oxygen transport
Visible brown NO₂ only with no CO relevance
Nephelometric turbidity of drinking water
Leachate from open dumps only

questions.expl: Correct (a): CO sources and toxicity via combustion. (b)–(d) are wrong pollutants/media.

questions.text: Asbestos in indoor air discussions is hazardous chiefly because:

choices.text: Inhaled fibers can cause lung damage and cancer; historically used in tiles and insulation
It neutralizes all greenhouse gases on contact
It measures dissolved oxygen in rivers
It is the main component of clean dry air at 21%

questions.expl: Correct (a): fiber inhalation risk from building materials. (b)–(d) are nonsense in context.

questions.text: The WHO ambient database example ranking includes which Philippine monitoring context cited in slides?

choices.text: NIA Road, Philippines appearing in a global PM concentration list (2016 table)
Only Kanpur, India with no Philippine sites
Only marine Class SA shellfish waters
Only PNSDW chlorine residuals

questions.expl: Correct (a): NIA Road reference in WHO table slide. (b)–(d) omit or misplace the Philippine datapoint.
refs: WHO Global Ambient Air Quality Database (cited in lecture)

questions.text: Water vapor in the atmosphere (lecture notes) is significant because it:

choices.text: Acts as a heat-transfer agent with spatial variability (e.g., lower polar fractions vs equatorial)
Comprises a fixed 78% of dry air by volume
Eliminates all photochemical smog without sunlight
Is identical to suspended PM₂.₅ metals

questions.expl: Correct (a): vapor as heat-transfer medium with latitude contrast. (b) confuses with N₂. (c)–(d) misassign roles.

questions.text: Tropospheric ozone in photochemical smog is beneficial when it replaces stratospheric ozone entirely—there is no distinction in impacts between layers.
questions.expl: FALSE: lecture treats tropospheric ozone in smog as harmful irritant distinct from stratospheric UV-shield discourse elsewhere. TRUE would collapse layer-specific impacts incorrectly.

questions.text: Lead in particulate/air pollution pathways in the slides is associated with:

choices.text: Historical gasoline/paint sources, soil contamination, and severe neurological/toxic outcomes
Only beneficial micronutrient enrichment without dose response
Only water turbidity NTU calibration
Only eutrophication of lakes

questions.expl: Correct (a): Pb toxicity and exposure routes per PM discussion. (b)–(d) misassign media/effects.

questions.text: Integrated interpretation: reducing mobile and stationary fossil combustion in a city most directly targets which lecture pollutant families?

choices.text: NOx, SO₂, PM, and photochemical smog precursors
Only waterborne cholera vibrios
Only landfill leachate metals without air overlap
Only indoor radon without outdoor combustion

questions.expl: Correct (a): fossil combustion ties to major air pollutant groups taught. (b)–(d) are other environmental compartments.

questions.text: An analyst argues that “waste” is epistemically different from natural detritus. Which reasoning best matches the lecture framing?

choices.text: Because silicate minerals lack biological decay pathways, they are the archetype of waste
Because biodegradation is absent globally, any uneaten leaf is waste
Because humans assign discard status to materials while ecosystems route elements through biogeochemical cycles
Because only urban households generate materials that leave the technosphere

questions.expl: Correct (c): Lec 5.4 treats waste as anthropogenic discard status versus natural cycling. (a) confuses persistence with waste definition. (b) denies biodegradation. (d) narrows generators.
refs: Smith & Smith (1998) Elements of Ecology (optional cross-check)

questions.text: A solid-waste inventory lumps “municipal refuse” for barangay budgeting. Which characterization most faithfully tracks Lec 5.4?

choices.text: Tailings + fly ash arising solely from precious-metal smelting campaigns
Commingled refuse from residential households and commerce-based generators
Regulated biomedical sharps streams only
Post-harvest lignocellulosic residues attributable only to tillage

questions.expl: Correct (b): municipal MSW in Lec 5.4 pairs household and commercial discards. (a) aligns with industrial mining waste, not municipal. (c) isolates biomedical without general municipal mix. (d) is agricultural residue, a different management silo.

questions.text: Environmental officers must tag “industrial solid waste” in a DENR report. Which sourcing narrative is most defensible?

choices.text: Administrative clerical paper from head-office finance
Process outputs, scrap, and residuals from manufacturing/industrial activity
Domestic meal preparation only
Seasonal park horticultural trimmings only

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 5.4 attributes industrial waste to production lines and plant operations. (a) shades toward commercial office waste, (c) toward household, (d) toward municipal green waste—each mislabels the industrial category.

questions.text: Identify the broadest defensible statement about hazardous wastes in the Philippine lecture examples.

choices.text: They may stem only from PCB manufacturing with no household analogues
They are confined to Class I hospital red-bag streams exclusively
They can originate from households, industrial facilities, or hospitals when toxic substances concentrate
They exclude organics entirely if pH is neutral

questions.expl: Correct (c): Lec 5.4 emphasizes multiple generator classes once toxics are present. (a)/(b) arbitrarily restrict sources. (d) is chemically naïve—hazard classification is not pH-only.

questions.text: Because pathogen or sharp injury risk can attend clinical discards, biomedical/hospital wastes are treated in the lecture taxonomy as potentially infectious even when source reduction is practiced.
questions.expl: TRUE: infectious biomedical categories reflect both chemical and biological hazards; source reduction does not remove infection potential from sharps/soiled materials. Misreading FALSE implies hospitals never generate infectious residuals—contradicts Lec 5.4 risk framing.

questions.text: Republic Act No. 9003 is formally identified in its own Section 1 heading as which statute title?

choices.text: Republic Act No. 6969 — Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act
Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999 (RA 8749)
Renewable Energy Act of 2008 (RA 9513)

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 5.4 gives the short title "Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000" for RA 9003. (a) is RA 6969. (c) is the Clean Air Act. (d) is the Renewable Energy Act.

questions.text: Per CvSU Lec 5.4, on which date was Republic Act No. 9003 enacted according to the lecture slides?

choices.text: 16 February 2001
26 January 2001
11 June 1978
26 January 2000

questions.expl: Correct (a): Lec 5.4 states RA 9003 was enacted on February 16, 2001. (b)–(d) are distractors from other statutes or common mismatches.

questions.text: Which policy declaration for RA 9003 is summarized in Lec 5.4?

choices.text: Nationwide criminalization of every polymer regardless of recycling potential
Adopt a systematic, comprehensive, ecological solid waste program protecting public health and the environment
Nationalize all informal recovery networks without due process
Eliminate material recovery facilities to centralize landfills only

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 5.4 frames RA 9003 as providing a legal framework for systematic, comprehensive ecological solid-waste management protecting health and environment. (a)/(c)/(d) caricature goals not stated on the slides.

questions.text: Implementation of RA 9003 in the lecture hinges on nested institutions. Which grouping most completely matches the lecturer’s emphasis?

choices.text: NSWMC, National Ecology Center, and local Solid Waste Management Boards
Barangay captains acting without higher-tier policy bodies
UN Security Council peacekeeping units
Solely the World Bank safeguards office

questions.expl: Correct (a): Lec 5.4 aligns with RA 9003’s national–local governance stack (NSWMC, NEC, SWMBs). (b) ignores national policy architecture. (c)/(d) invoke irrelevant global bodies for domestic SWM mandates.

questions.text: Metro Manila household share of waste near ~74% reflects NSWMC-sourced slide data in Lec 5.4 and should be refreshed against the latest NSWMC reports—not treated as a universal constant outside the capital.
questions.expl: TRUE: the slide cites that domestic share; verifying against updated NSWMC dashboards is good practice. Claiming FALSE denies the lecturer’s cited statistic without offering counter-data.

questions.text: Climate communications require disciplining vocabulary. Which formulation best matches WMO/IPCC-style climatology framing used in Lec 5.5?

choices.text: The noon wind vector at a rooftop site
Statistical description of long-period weather, often using ~30-year reference windows
Synoptic description of a derecho event only
Next week’s newspaper forecast headline

questions.expl: Correct (b): climate is the distribution of weather over multi-decadal baselines. (a)/(c) depict instantaneous or event-scale dynamics. (d) is media-scale prediction, not climatology.
refs: IPCC AR6 WGI Annex (baseline periods) (optional cross-check)

questions.text: Contrast weather and climate for a policy briefing. Which pairing is analytically sound?

choices.text: Weather is always defined as exactly 365 daily samples
Weather is instantaneous to synoptic-scale atmospheric state; climate is its long-run statistics
They are identical constructs differing only in map projection
Weather solely measures relative humidity with no temperature signal

questions.expl: Correct (b): standard glossaries separate short-lived state from distributional summaries. (a) invents rigid sample lengths. (c) denies meaningful scale separation. (d) omits multifield weather definition.

questions.text: Which pair most closely aligns with anthropogenic greenhouse-gas narratives foregrounded alongside CO₂ in the climate lecture?

choices.text: N₂ and Ar as dominant forcing agents
O₂ and H₂ bonding pairs dominating infrared opacity
CO₂ and CH₄ owing to volumetric forcing and methane’s strong per-molecule potency
He dominating stratospheric ozone chemistry

questions.expl: Correct (c): Lec 5.5 + IPCC cite CO₂ longevity and CH₄ potency among key non-CO₂ forcers. (a) lists inert major constituents with weak GHG roles. (b)/(d) misassign radiatively active gases.

questions.text: Describe the ice–albedo loop when sea-ice retreats. Which mechanism captures the positive feedback emphasized in class?

choices.text: Additional ice nuclei always raise planetary albedo irrespective of latitude
Loss of high-albedo ice exposes darker ocean that absorbs more shortwave, accelerating melt
Open water whitens uniformly, raising albedo
Cloud decks vanish entirely within 24 h of any melt event

questions.expl: Correct (b): classic ice–albedo feedback in cryosphere chapters. (a) ignores sign of change. (c) reverses ocean reflectance. (d) overstates cloud coupling.

questions.text: Article 2 of the Paris Agreement is summarized in Lec 5.5. Which numeric guardrail pairing is faithful?

choices.text: Hold increase well below 2 °C while pursuing efforts toward 1.5 °C
Allow unchecked warming through 5 °C before policy review
Avoid numeric temperature objectives entirely
Mandate return to pre-industrial means within five years globally

questions.expl: Correct (a): matches UNFCCC Art.2 long-term temperature goal. (b)–(d) contradict treaty text or feasibility.

questions.text: Under the Paris Agreement’s procedural rhythm, successive NDC communications and the global stocktake embed roughly five-year cadences even though domestic policy may move faster or slower.
questions.expl: TRUE: Treaty architecture pairs periodic submissions/stocktake with multi-year cycles despite national variance. FALSE would deny structured international review periods.

questions.text: Evaluate deforestation as a coupled carbon-cycle perturbation—not merely a land-cover tweak.

choices.text: It uniformly brightens planetary albedo because all forests are darker than oceans
It emits carbon from disturbed biomass/soils and trims future uptake capacity
It removes atmospheric O₂ outright, causing instant hypoxia
It terminates tropospheric moisture convergence globally

questions.expl: Correct (b): AFOLU emissions + lost sink potential dominate IPCC narratives. (a) oversimplifies spectral albedo feedbacks. (c) exaggerates O₂ drawdown. (d) confuses local hydroclimate with global shutdown.

questions.text: Which operational definition of “solid waste management” captures the full chain stressed in Lec 5.4 rather than a single end-point?

choices.text: Exclusive reliance on engineered landfilling without upstream controls
Systematic control from generation through storage, collection, transport, separation, processing, recycling, recovery, and disposal
Open burning as the sole sanctioned treatment modality
Export brokering regardless of destination environmental safeguards

questions.expl: Correct (b): mirrors lecture’s life-cycle control framing. (a)/(c)/(d) each collapse the chain to a single controversial tactic.

questions.text: Interpret the regression-style findings of the cited General Trias household waste survey. Which covariance story matches the lecturer’s inference?

choices.text: Household size showed the strongest statistical association with discarded mass among tested sociodemographics
Years of schooling per adult remained the strongest positive driver even when income fixed effects were applied
Waste masses scaled with lunar phase through tidal effects on collection trucks
Administrative toponym length served as a proxy for economic complexity and explained variance best

questions.expl: Correct (a): slides flag family size as highly significant while educational attainment was not significant in that comparison—do not over-extrapolate beyond the presented model. (b) contradicts the slide contrast. (c)/(d) import spurious mechanisms absent from the study frame.

questions.text: Macro-plastics lodged in waterways interact with floods and habitat quality per Lec integrations. Pick the causal chain least vulnerable to methodological critique.

choices.text: Polyethylene density forbids flotation, so canals cannot surcharge
Improper disposal increases fluvial plastics → constricted hydraulic capacity plus chemical vectoring → compounded flood/ecosystem risks layering on climate sensitivities
Self-purifying river metabolism mineralizes polyethylene within hours absent sunlight
Solid-waste burdens are orthogonal to drainage performance if NDC pledges exist

questions.expl: Correct (b): couples structural blockage + pollution stress with broader crisis framing as in Nathanson/Katyal-style pollution pathway pedagogy. (a) denies basic buoyancy/mechanics. (c) overstates biochemical weathering. (d) falsely decouples local hydraulics from waste.

questions.text: If higher-income cohorts in the lecture’s 2016 comparison generated ~0.50 kg/cap/day versus ~0.34 kg/cap/day in the lower bracket, the gap is consistent with consumption-intensity explanations but must be caveated by sample geography and survey vintage.
questions.expl: TRUE: differential waste intensity often tracks purchasing power and packaging-rich diets—yet correlation ≠ universal law; controls for tourism, metering error, etc., matter. FALSE would pretend the statistic is meaningless or fabricated without counter-evidence.

questions.text: In EIA logic, quantify “impact” relative to baseline trajectory—not relative to bookkeeping artifacts.

choices.text: The approved Environmental Management Plan line-item cashflow
The attributable deviation of environmental/social parameters from baseline due to proposed activity
The ECC’s nominal validity window before reapplication
The ceremonial construction start date

questions.expl: Correct (b): impact = Δ(baseline→with project) attributable to actions; aligns with Canter/WB texts. (a) mixes financing with causal change. (c) imports administrative timelines. (d) is unrelated to environmental change metrics.
refs: ADB / World Bank Environmental Assessment Sourcebooks (optional cross-check)

questions.text: Baselines for noise, river flow, or livelihoods should be documented as:

choices.text: A single grab sample taken on the driest Tuesday
A process with variability and trends over time—not merely a snapshot in time
Investor sentiment indices only
Equity market volatility series unrelated to the site

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 6 defines baseline as existing conditions with variability and trend over time, not a single snapshot. (a) courts false negatives/positives. (c)/(d) import irrelevant economic signals.

questions.text: Screening an expressway cannot credibly ignore social/cultural receptors, public health endpoints, and fiscal externalities even when biophysics dominates headlines.
questions.expl: TRUE: integrated EIA explicitly cross-walks sectors in Lec 6. FALSE would reduce IA to one-dimensional biology, contradicting lecture scoping.

questions.text: Agencies emphasize “most significant impacts” because:

choices.text: Analyst teams enjoy unlimited person-months for every dust particle
Analytic capacity is bounded, so triage targets material effects that drive decisions
Minor externalities are definitionally zero by RA decree
Philippine law bans impact matrices outright

questions.expl: Correct (b): screening/scoping rationality under DENR/ADB practice. (a) ignores budget/time. (c) is false. (d) misstates tools available.

questions.text: Presidential Decree No. 1586 (1978) created which national environmental assessment architecture?

choices.text: The Renewable Portfolio Standard under the DOE
The Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System
Republic Act No. 9003 solid waste rules
The U.S. Federal Clean Water Act permitting matrix

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 6 states PD 1586 established the Environmental Impact Statement System. (a) is energy policy. (c) is solid-waste legislation. (d) is a foreign statute.

questions.text: Under PD 1151’s policy logic, which trigger most faithfully forces deeper environmental documentation?

choices.text: Proposals certified a priori as environmentally neutral without study
Undertakings that may significantly affect environmental quality
Any school building regardless of scale or siting
Projects below an arbitrary ₱50,000 invoice cap always

questions.expl: Correct (b): PD 1151 frames significant-effect screening; Lec 6 cites it. (a) negates the policy purpose. (c)/(d) overbroad/underbroad without categorical rules.

questions.text: Category D projects in the DENR typology described in lecture are understood as:

choices.text: Always ECC-mandatory mega-infrastructure regardless of screening
Presumed unlikely to cause significant adverse environmental effects and ordinarily outside ECC coverage under evaluated rules
Required to locate solely inside ECAs for monitoring convenience
Automatically classified as toxic bulk handling

questions.expl: Correct (b): matches orientation materials on low-risk categories—still verify current DAO lists. (a) confuses with Cat A/B. (c)/(d) invent requirements.

questions.text: An Environmental Compliance Certificate from DENR–EMB conceptually attests that:

choices.text: Statutes no longer bind once the certificate is framed
The proponent met PEISS requirements subject to conditions that reduce adverse effects
Environmental monitoring is optional unless neighbors complain
All other LGU permits are preempted without further review

questions.expl: Correct (b): ECC is conditional compliance certification, not immunity. (a)/(c)/(d) misstate legal effect—other permits and laws still apply.

questions.text: Classroom slides echo DENR trainer excerpts that ECCs may lapse if implementation does not commence within roughly five years unless extensions or new evaluations apply.
questions.expl: TRUE: conditional validity is common in ECC guidance—confirm current memoranda. FALSE would treat ECCs as perpetual blank checks.

questions.text: Place the lecture’s EIA sequencing: which step gates whether later predictions even target the right stressors?

choices.text: Post-audit after decommissioning only
Scoping that frames issues, alternatives, and spatial/temporal boundaries
Initial public offering of corporate shares
Mechanical groundbreaking before baseline walkover

questions.expl: Correct (b): scoping is step 1 in Lec 6 narrative. (a) is far downstream. (c)/(d) confound financial or construction events with IA design.

questions.text: Which bundle of methods does the lecture couple with defensible impact forecasting?

choices.text: Desktop horoscopes for construction months
Expert elicitation, analog case reviews, field experiments, and quantitative models
Randomized coin allocation of significance ratings
Colorimetric preference tests for baseline maps

questions.expl: Correct (b): mirrors Lec 6 + standard env. engineering references. (a)/(c)/(d) are non-evidentiary thought experiments.

questions.text: A credible EMP must embed both mitigation hierarchies and measurable monitoring indicators rather than aspirational slogans alone.
questions.expl: TRUE: lecture emphasizes mitigation + monitoring + reporting threads. FALSE would omit accountability mechanisms.

questions.text: WCED’s (1987) sustainability anchor stresses inter-temporal fairness. Which wording is canonical?

choices.text: Optimize quarterly EBIT without externalities
Meet present needs without compromising future generations’ ability to meet their own needs
Halt industrial metabolism entirely for a generation
Ban every renewable subsidy to preserve fossils

questions.expl: Correct (b): Brundtland definition verbatim in teaching materials. (a) ignores externalities/intergenerational ethics. (c)/(d) are straw positions.

questions.text: How many Sustainable Development Goals sit in the 2030 Agenda framework referenced in lecture?

choices.text: 10 goals tied only to biodiversity
15 goals covering OECD members exclusively
17 interconnected goals spanning social, environmental, economic targets
25 subsidiary targets with no headline goals

questions.expl: Correct (c): UN lists 17 SDGs adopted 2015. (a)/(b)/(d) misstate architecture.

questions.text: Operationalizing sustainability simultaneously trades off prosperity, ecological integrity, and social inclusion rather than maximizing one pillar obliviously.
questions.expl: TRUE: triple-pillar rhetoric in Lec 7 parallels UN discourse; ignoring trade-offs collapses realism. FALSE pretends single-metric fixes suffice universally.
refs: Kaneko et al. (2014) sustainable living narratives (optional cross-check)

questions.text: HDI in Lec 7 is a composite measure. Which third pillar joins life expectancy and education in the slides?

choices.text: Military expenditure as % of GDP
Income
National social-media follower totals
Exclusive economic zone nautical miles

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 7 lists HDI factors as life expectancy, education, and income. (a)/(c)/(d) are not in the lecture composite.

questions.text: Cleaner production (lecture/UUNEP lineage) principally targets:

choices.text: Brand palette redesign without process change
Source reductions in materials, energy, emissions, wastewater, noise, and waste heat at process level
Additional tertiary packaging layers to signal luxury
End-of-pipe dilution exclusively without prevention

questions.expl: Correct (b): prevention/integration focus of CP. (a)/(c) superficial. (d) contradicts cleaner-production hierarchy.

questions.text: Identify the lecturer’s renewable archetype among these dispatchable/low-carbon options.

choices.text: Peat-fired steam plant fed by ancient bog carbon
High-temperature geothermal binary or flash plant tapping crustal heat
Sub-bituminous baseload steam without CCS
Steam-assisted gravity drainage of shale bitumen

questions.expl: Correct (b): geothermal enumerated with solar/wind/hydro/biomass renewables in notes. (a)/(c)/(d) remain fossil/high-carbon in practice.

questions.text: Ecological footprint accounting contrasts:

choices.text: Psychometric IQ with national laureates
Resources and land required to sustain consumption versus available biocapacity
Equity volatility indices only
A-weighted roadway noise contours alone

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 7 defines ecological footprint as resources/land needed to sustain consumption patterns and compare ecological demands. Other options are unrelated metrics.

questions.text: Agricultural residuals from harvest, pruning, or post-processing fit the lecturer’s agricultural solid-waste strand even though quantities swing seasonally.
questions.expl: TRUE: cropping/harvest wastes appear in sectoral taxonomy. FALSE would wrongly limit agriculture to manure only.

questions.text: Commercial solid waste streams in Lec 5.4 originate from establishments that:

choices.text: Operate pyrometallurgical refining as their core SKU
May retail or administer services without being factories per se—shops, malls, offices
Fish capture exclusively on EEZ fleets
Hold exclusive nuclear-material licenses

questions.expl: Correct (b): commercial wastes cover non-production commerce. (a)/(c)/(d) target industrial/fisheries/nuclear special cases—not the lecturer’s definitional gist.

questions.text: ECA inventories in lectures overlap sensitive landscapes. Pick the collage matching slide exemplars:

choices.text: Generic indoor office floors without heightened ecological services
Watershed reservations, sanctuaries, coral reefs/mangroves, aquifer recharge tracts among others per PP 2146 lineage
Arid dune belts lacking regulatory protection
Any speculative mall footprint regardless of wetland adjacency

questions.expl: Correct (b): mirrors ECA slideshow—verify enumerated lists legally. (a)/(c)/(d) either too ordinary or speculative.

questions.text: Mega dams or major fossil/renewable power stations exemplify:

choices.text: Category D negligible-risk hobby farms
Environmentally Critical Projects with disproportionate footprints
Projects inherently exempt from all environmental statutes
Household compost pilot sites

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 6 uses them as ECP exemplars needing scrutiny. Others mis-slot risk classes.

questions.text: Spatial scoping must bound where effects manifest. Choose the academically faithful combination:

choices.text: Corporate headquarters floorplate exclusively
Development footprint plus primary & secondary influence zones and optional regional corridors for cumulative stressors
Orbital altitudes unaffected by terrestrial projects
Indeterminate boundary because GIS optional

questions.expl: Correct (b): multi-tier AOI language of Lec 6. Others trivialize geometry.

questions.text: Judging significance weaves ecological and social strands. Pick the analytic triplet highlighted in lecture:

choices.text: Lobby paint shear selection only
Statistical expectancy/magnitude, organizational level affected, perceived social stakes
Astrological house positions of decision makers
CPU benchmarking scores unrelated to ecology

questions.expl: Correct (b): matches significance discussion. Others are caricatures.

questions.text: Deconstructing an “activity” (e.g., highway) into concrete “actions” (survey, blasting, runoff controls) improves attribution of baseline deviations to specific constructors.
questions.expl: TRUE: hierarchical pairing appears in Lec 6 methodological guidance—FALSE collapses causal clarity.

questions.text: Circular-economy strategy in lectures stresses:

choices.text: Maximizing single-use polymers to inflate GDP
Minimize waste and maximize resource efficiency while reducing virgin resource use
Linear cradle-to-grave default without feedback
Exclusive reliance on third-country landfill

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 7 circular-economy slides stress minimizing wastes, maximizing resource efficiency, and reducing finite resource use. (a)/(c)/(d) contradict that framing.
refs: UNEP / EU Circular Economy Action Plan (context) (optional cross-check)

questions.text: Yale/Columbia EPI is pedagogically summarized as:

choices.text: Gamified leaderboard without peer review
Multi-indicator aggregation ranking national environmental performance
GDP per capita rebranded green
Soil taxonomy reference cards only

questions.expl: Correct (b): composite index rationale from lecture + EPI site. Others mis-characterize methodology.

questions.text: The natural greenhouse effect describes radiatively active gases impeding outbound longwave flux; intensifying their concentrations strengthens forcing unless offset by feedbacks or aerosols.
questions.expl: TRUE: basic radiative-transfer framing per IPCC glossaries plus Lec 5.5. FALSE omits foundational physics.

questions.text: Photochemical smog in Lec 5.3 includes tropospheric ozone formed in sunlight. Tropospheric O₃ in urban afternoons is best classified as:

choices.text: A primary pollutant exiting tailpipes unchanged
A secondary product of precursor chemistry (e.g., NOx and VOCs in sunlight)
Unrelated to air-quality management narratives
Only meaningful if dissolved in groundwater

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 5.3 lists tropospheric ozone among photochemical smog products formed in the presence of sunlight. (a) mislabels tailpipe primaries. (c)/(d) confuse media.

questions.text: Per Lec 5.5, both carbon dioxide and methane are named among greenhouse gases linked to enhanced radiative trapping.
questions.expl: TRUE: Lec 5.5 greenhouse-gas lists include carbon dioxide and methane among key contributors. FALSE would contradict the slide inventory.
refs: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch.5 / Ch.7 (optional cross-check)

questions.text: EIA as a planning tool (Lec 6) means mitigation and project design should occur:

choices.text: Only after abandonment when bonds mature
During planning and design—where to locate projects and how to design them—before commitments foreclose alternatives
Behind closed doors excluding stakeholders entirely
Solely when ODA co-financing triggers safeguard templates

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 6 presents EIA as a planning tool for siting, design, and minimizing adverse impacts before operational lock-in. (a)/(c)/(d) mis-time or mis-scope the process.

questions.text: Per Lec 6, Presidential Decree No. 1586 (1978) established which nationwide environmental assessment architecture?
questions.expl: TRUE: Lec 6 cites PD 1586 as establishing the Environmental Impact Statement System. FALSE would misplace PEISS inception.

questions.text: Technical review of impact predictions scrutinizes:

choices.text: Deleting measured baselines whenever models disagree modestly
Models’ assumptions, data pedigree, magnitude claims, plausibility under uncertainty
Substitution of ECC applications for BIR tax forms
Cancellation of all monitoring KPIs preemptively

questions.expl: Correct (b): QA commonplace in Glasson texts + Lec 6. Others describe malpractice.
refs: Glasson et al. Introduction to EIA (optional cross-check)

questions.text: Early consultation narrows disputed facts, distributes mitigation burdens transparently, and can increase legitimacy even when projects proceed.
questions.expl: TRUE: IAIA precepts echoed in Philippine practice briefs—FALSE denies deliberative gains.

questions.text: The WCED (1987) definition in Lec 7 implies intergenerational equity requires that development:

choices.text: Maximize quarterly profit without regard to environmental limits
Meet present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own needs
Halt all industrial activity for one generation
Ban renewable energy subsidies entirely

questions.expl: Correct (b): Lec 7 quotes sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations. (a)/(c)/(d) contradict the slide definition.

questions.text: Per Lec 7, how are the UN Sustainable Development Goals characterized?

choices.text: Seventeen interlinked objectives forming a shared blueprint for people and the planet
Ten goals tied only to biodiversity
Fifteen goals covering OECD members exclusively
Twenty-five subsidiary targets with no headline goals

questions.expl: Correct (a): Lec 7 describes seventeen interlinked SDGs as a shared blueprint. (b)–(d) misstate the count or scope taught in-session.

questions.text: MPI as taught bundles overlapping deprivations in:

choices.text: NASDAQ tickers correlated with UNDP HQ latitude
Health, education, living-standard dimensions weighted per OPHI/UNDP
Currency arbitrage exposures only
Satellite-TV channel counts

questions.expl: Correct (b): MPI pillar documentation. Others nonsense metrics.

questions.text: Gender Inequality Index remains a sanctioned HDR composite marrying reproductive-health, empowerment, and labor-market inequality signals.
questions.expl: TRUE UNDP technical documentation; FALSE denies published metric.

questions.text: Engineered landfills leak leachate when liners fail or ponds overflow. Conceptually why is leachate the policy headache?

choices.text: It improves rooftop RF propagation
It transports dissolved metals/organics into groundwater/surface receptors
It catalytically heals stratospheric ozone holes
It chemically scrubs fugitive methane to zero unconditionally

questions.expl: Correct (b): pathway to water-quality impairment in solid-waste engineering primers. Others physically implausible hype.

questions.text: RA 9003’s declared policies privilege ecological segregation, avoidance, recycling, recovery over indiscriminate dumping when lawful alternatives scale—yet prohibitions/detailed mandates appear later in the same Act.
questions.expl: TRUE reading §2 in context of operative articles; FALSE would caricature RA 9003 as aspirational fluff only.

questions.text: A CNC letter generally communicates:

choices.text: ECC demand persists categorically irrespective of CNC text
Under screened rules at filing time the project lacks ECC obligation though other permits endure
EIA study failed morally necessitating revocation
Automatic cessation of enterprise license without hearing

questions.expl: Correct (b): procedural meaning per EMB practice—still update DAO/MC knowledge. Others misstate juridical effect.

essays.title: Urban waste & environmental crises
essays.prompt: Integrate RA 9003 instruments with at least TWO environmental crisis dimensions (pollution, resource strain, vulnerability) using lecture waste statistics as evidence.
guide: Cite NSWMC/MM or national kg/cap/day only as in slides

essays.title: Baseline → Impact logic
essays.prompt: Explain how baseline variability affects impact significance for a hypothetical quarry in an ECA.
guide: Give one biophysical metric + one social

essays.title: ECC vs CNC
essays.prompt: Contrast when an ECC versus CNC pathway applies using Categories A–D.
guide: ECC conditions & validity rules from lecture

essays.title: EIA procedure map
essays.prompt: Sequence scoping→baseline→prediction→evaluation→EMP→review→ECC→monitoring and tie each step to ONE decision-maker need.

essays.title: WCED definition stress-test
essays.prompt: Argue whether high-carbon business-as-usual growth meets WCED sustainability; cite intergenerational equity.

essays.title: Measures & instruments
essays.prompt: Compare HDI versus Ecological Footprint as dashboards; link one SDG each to renewables and cleaner production.
